A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Long Grounded Thoughts and retain the same core synthesis pipeline and experiments. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original SFT, DPO, and GRPO experiments, dataset analyses, and transfer evaluations on MMLU-Pro, MMAU, and NiEH.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds semantic-diversity analysis, reasoning-trace ablations, and MathVision and VisuLogic results.

M1.justification: Object-grounded question generation, compositional hardening, VLM-to-LLM thought expansion, regex-constrained decoding, and preference construction remain unchanged. The newly evaluated short-CoT and direct-answer variants are ablation controls, not revisions to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: V2 adds MathVision and VisuLogic evaluation in Appendix A.7 and Table 9, extending coverage to visual mathematics, including mixed answer formats, and visual logic. DOCCI training and the existing vision, text, audio, and embodied evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: V2 Table 12 introduces a thinking-prompt-only comparator and direct-answer and short-CoT SFT controls against full-CoT training. Comparator membership in the established benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a diversity comparison using 1,000 questions from three shared images and a 750K-example Stage 1 reasoning-trace ablation. Existing judge-based versus rule-based evaluation and the NiEH input-window protocol are retained; detailed settings for MathVision and VisuLogic are not supplied.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an embedding/KDE analysis testing whether object grounding reduces question redundancy. Table 12 adds controlled comparisons of prompting, no-CoT, short-CoT, and full-CoT training. Together these substantially expand diagnostic evidence for two central design choices; earlier scaling analyses and qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 7 introduces Gaussian KDE contours labeled '95% confidence,' a new statistical reporting element whose confidence construction is not explained. Neither version reports benchmark uncertainty across repeated training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: V2 adds diversity findings, full reasoning-trace ablation results, and MathVision scores of 49.57 versus 51.77 and VisuLogic scores of 11.5 versus 19.3 for the base and trained models. Tables 4 and 7 revise SFT MMLU-Pro from 50.13 to 50.82, now above LPT's unchanged 50.77. The main vision table remains unchanged. NiEH's claimed gain is corrected from about 10 to 8.8 points without changing its table scores.

T1.justification: The formal question-generation relations, preference definitions, and appendix similarity and filtering equations are retained. New descriptive metrics and informal explanations do not introduce revised mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly promotes MCQ-to-open-ended generalization and the scale of its post-training study as main contributions. It qualifies offline RL from matching online RL to potentially matching or being competitive with it. The central synthesis, scaling, and cross-modal-transfer claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 strengthens the caption-collapse explanation using its diversity analysis and attributes short-CoT underperformance to low-fidelity reasoning. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning weaker non-MCQ instruction following and ambiguous synthesized questions while emphasizing robust open-ended transfer. These materially change the mechanism discussion and applicability boundaries; DOCCI dependence remains disclosed.

D1.justification: V2 documents sampling, embedding-model, and KDE choices for the new diversity analysis. It states that Stage 1 and Stage 2 subsets are released separately, replacing v1's generic publication-timed artifact-release statement. Existing generation prompts and principal training hyperparameters remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds Golden Goose and Privasis citations and removes the ProRL reference. It sharpens the comparison with LPT around synthesis saturation and cognitive simplicity, while retaining the same principal research lineage and compressing descriptions of other related methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial method and discussion passages are rewritten. V2 adds contribution bullets and a dedicated dataset-analysis subsection, folds RL synthesis into the method section, compresses related work, and replaces the limitations and reproducibility sections with an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main paper switches from one-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. V2 merges Table 4's two panels, moves v1 Table 3 to appendix Table 11, adds the diversity figure and new result tables, and adds a sum row to the cognitive-behavior table. Existing qualitative figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new CoT ablation and diversity analysis provide more direct evidence for previously weakly tested design rationales, and v2 corrects the NiEH gain and removes accompanying prose that contradicted Table 8. These benefits are tempered by sparse settings for the added benchmarks, stronger interpretations than the limited analyses establish, and removal of explicit non-MCQ and question-ambiguity limitations. The net improvement is useful but limited.
